text: The call came from an old friend who did not scare easy.
That told Reacher enough.
"Where?".
The answer took him to a hard little town with bad roads, cheap motels.
Men who watched strangers too closely.
Reacher liked places like that fine.
They showed their teeth early.
The men never saw him coming.
The driver went down first.
The passenger tried to move, but the seat belt slowed him just enough.
They had followed the wrong man.
The phone led him to a warehouse outside town.
It looked empty from the road.
Then he found the fresh tire tracks.
The tracks were wide and deep.
Heavy machine.
Loaded going in.
Lighter coming out.
The team had been there, and they had not gone quietly.
Reacher found a second guard near the office.
This one was awake enough to reach for a weapon.
Bad men should not do paperwork.
The address was twenty miles away.
Reacher got there on foot, by bus, and by stolen time.
Two trucks blocked the road.
Four men stepped into the light.
One had a shotgun.
One had a bat.
The other two had the nervous look of men who had been told this would be easy.
The man followed it.
The other two tried to rush him together.
That was almost thoughtful.
The team was close, and so was the end of the men holding them.
The team was in an old barn past the tree line.
Reacher saw guards at the door, light through the boards, and movement inside.
Now he knew where most of them were.
The first guard went down without a sound.
The second turned at the wrong moment and joined him.
Reacher took the weapon, checked the door, and stepped inside.
The room snapped toward him.
That was a poor choice.
The knife man hit the wall and stayed there.
The barn went still.
Then he led the team out into the dark.
